title: The Weight of a Stone
logline: A cutter turns a rough stone once under a lamp and says in a second what it is worth, a judgement that took a lifetime to become instant.
human_question: What has to happen, in an instant, for someone to simply know what they are looking at?

situation.what_happens: Rough and cut stones pass through a working day and each one has to be judged: tilted to the light, turned in the fingers, bought, rejected, or assigned a way of cutting that cannot be undone once the wheel touches it. The judgements are made in about a second each, and the money in them is large relative to everything else in the trade. Sometimes two people who both know the work disagree about the same stone, and the disagreement has to be settled by somebody paying.
situation.who_is_involved: The cutter or sorter whose eye the trade pays for; a buyer with their own opinion and their own money; whoever dug or washed the stone, who is usually furthest from the price; and a learner who can see that a verdict was reached but not how.
situation.what_is_at_stake: The value of a single stone, which can be a large part of a month. A reputation that exists only as a record of having been right quickly. And for the learner, whether a judgement that lives entirely inside someone else's eye can be passed on at all.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A stone arrives, is judged, and is bought, refused or cut, usually the same day. The pressures are the light, the buyer's own view, the money already committed and the irreversibility of cutting. It ends in a stone worth more than it was, worth less, or ruined, and the trade, not the film, decides which.

concept_merge.why_together: C041 contributes the fullest form of the sources' process, the one that runs when the sense, the object, the light and the attention are all strong together: the resting mind is disturbed, turns toward, bare seeing occurs, then receiving, investigating and determining, then a burst of full engagement and a short lingering. C036 contributes what the eye is actually given in that run, a blend of colour and never the ruby, the flaw or the price. C039 contributes why such a judgement has to be fast or not at all, since matter's own lifespan is short and the whole process is built to fit inside it. A verdict given under a lamp in one second is the one everyday situation where all four of C041's conditions are deliberately arranged by the worker.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they show that the practised eye is not seeing more than anyone else. It is receiving the same bare colour and adding a lifetime of naming to it, inside a window the sources say is fixed by the material rather than by the person. The trained verdict looks like insight and is described by the sources as a relay.

concept_links.why: The digest sets out the fullest eye-door process and names its four conditions, a strong eye-sensitivity, a strong visible object, strong light and strong attention, all present together [C041-P:L25], followed by the seventeen-moment order of adverting, seeing, receiving, investigating, determining, seven moments of impulsion and two of registration [C041-P:L29-L48]. A lamp held close over a stone is a worker deliberately arranging those conditions. The digest's limits are held: the seventeen moments are not a neuroscience timing and may not be presented as milliseconds; 'the pause between stimulus and response is where your freedom lies' is a modern slogan the digest rules out by name; and the concluding burst is called wholesome, unwholesome or merely functional by the sources, never 'choice', which is the series' own reading.

The digest is explicit that the eye meets only colour, a blend of the colours of many clusters, not a stone and not a flaw, and that recognition comes from marks learned in earlier seeing [C036-P:L37-L41; C036-M:L9]. A snap verdict on a stone is built entirely in that gap. The digest also notes an unresolved tension in the source, which calls the visible object 'unmixed' in one place and a mixture of many clusters' colours in another [C036-P:L61; C036-P:L41]; the film does not choose between them.

The digest gives matter a lifespan of seventeen mind-moments against the mind's one, and says in plain terms that the world holds still for about as long as it takes to be noticed once [C039-M:L5; C039-P:L31]. That is the sources' own reason why a full judgement happens fast or not at all. The digest's guards apply: the clusters are not atoms, molecules or cells, and 'less than a hundred-thousandth of an eye-blink' is a traditional image and not a figure to quote as science.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: A judgement that looks instantaneous is, on these texts' account, a short relay of separate steps, and what the eye contributes to it is only colour. Everything that makes the verdict valuable, the name, the grade and the price, was added from what the person had already seen thousands of times before.
what_must_be_real: Real stones, real money and the trade's real secrecy. No verdict staged or repeated for the camera, and nothing filmed that would expose confidential pricing, sourcing or a participant's security. The cutter's own account of what a first look tells them, and what only a second look does, must lead.
position_hint: middle: its substance now sits inside the group's film about skilled work rather than holding a slot of its own, and it belongs wherever that film belongs.
risks: Glamorising a high-value trade without the labour and the mining behind it.
Implying valuations or trade secrets on camera in ways that put someone at risk.
Presenting a seventeen-moment count as a measured reaction time.
Treating a trained verdict as intuition or a sixth sense rather than as accumulated recognition.
drop_if: No trader or cutter will allow real transactions to be filmed.
Security around valuable stones makes honest filming impossible.
The work cannot be shown without exposing confidential pricing or sourcing.

connections.note: Its instant-verdict situation and its C036 link on colour arriving before any name now sit inside IDEA-0073, which needed a real trade to be about.
Both watch a trained eye separate raw colour from a name and a value, one under a lamp and one in half-light.

selection.reason: Folded into IDEA-0073, whose situation was abstract and which now carries this film's instant judgement, its years of accumulated recognition and its C036 link.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
